people.name: Angela

evidence.excerpt: Returns. Last holiday season. Buy online, return in store.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Trigger of the evaluation: holiday returns problem.

evidence.excerpt: The store couldn't see the online order, so staff were refunding to gift cards or telling people to mail it back.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Concrete failure in store returns, relayed by rep.

evidence.excerpt: they'd just launched a loyalty program that was supposed to work everywhere and didn't, because store and web were two different customer records.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Loyalty program broke due to split customer records.

evidence.excerpt: Their COO, Angela, apparently stood in a store on December 27th watching the returns queue.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Hedged with 'apparently'; hearsay about Angela.

evidence.excerpt: That's the story everybody there tells.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Customer lore, secondhand.

evidence.excerpt: The CTO, Raj. He ran the RFP, he was my contact the whole way.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Rep's first answer on decider; later contradicted.

evidence.excerpt: This is secondhand. Raj told me afterwards.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Competitor account comes from Raj after the fact.

evidence.excerpt: they came in with a retail team, people who'd done store rollouts, and they talked about one platform for the tills and the website, on one contract.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Raj
evidence.note: Raj's report of competitor pitch: retail team, one platform, one contract.

evidence.excerpt: And they named retailers Angela knew.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Raj
evidence.note: Competitor used references familiar to Angela.

evidence.excerpt: Before, it was all web. Conversion, checkout, wallets. After, it was stores.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Customer questions shifted from web to stores after meeting competitor.

evidence.excerpt: Raj forwarded me a list of 14 questions and 11 of them were about stores.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Concrete number: 11 of 14 questions about stores.

evidence.excerpt: How do you roll out 120 stores.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Scale: 120 stores; rollout question.

evidence.excerpt: Reaction: the online checkout demo. Their ecommerce lead loved it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Online checkout demo got positive reaction.

evidence.excerpt: Silence: the unified commerce part.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Unified commerce pitch got no reaction.

evidence.excerpt: Online and in-store on one platform, the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Our slide wording for unified commerce.

evidence.excerpt: "that's a diagram."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Bev
evidence.note: Bev dismissed the unified commerce slide.

evidence.excerpt: Then she asked how a return works. Step by step. At the till.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Bev wanted a concrete return walkthrough.

evidence.excerpt: I described it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Rep described rather than showed the return.

evidence.excerpt: Nobody on our side had run a store rollout.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Capability gap at store ops workshop.

evidence.excerpt: When Bev asked who does the installs, I said we'd bring in a partner. She wrote something down and didn't ask another question.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Partner answer on installs; Bev went quiet.

evidence.excerpt: I knew on the drive home.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Rep's sense the deal was lost after workshop.

evidence.excerpt: Right before that, honestly, we were ahead. Raj said so. We'd won the web side.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Rep claims lead before workshop; Raj said so; web side won.

evidence.excerpt: They had six people from store operations.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Customer brought six store ops people to workshop.

evidence.excerpt: Angela's team. Stores.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Angela's team requested the workshop.

evidence.excerpt: Angela.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Angela signed with Adyen.

evidence.excerpt: ...Probably Angela. Raj wanted us. I think. He told me he did.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Rep revises decider to Angela, hedged; Raj's preference per Raj.

evidence.excerpt: Once. The kickoff.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Rep met actual signer only once.

evidence.excerpt: We sent a case study. Fashion retailer, stores and online, good story.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Case study sent in place of a reference call.

evidence.excerpt: "can I talk to them?"
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela
evidence.note: Angela wanted a live reference.

evidence.excerpt: we couldn't set up a call in time.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: No reference call delivered.

evidence.excerpt: Then a rollout plan. Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Customer asked for a rollout plan.

evidence.excerpt: They wanted to watch an online order get returned at a store till, live. We described it. We never showed it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Live return demo requested, never shown.

evidence.excerpt: "One system for the tills and the website."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Bev
evidence.note: Bev's repeated phrase for the problem.

evidence.excerpt: "I don't want two vendors pointing at each other."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela

evidence.excerpt: "one customer, one basket."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Angela
evidence.note: Angela's phrase for unified customer and cart.

evidence.excerpt: They never said "unified commerce." We kept saying "in-person payments" and "point of sale." They said "the tills."
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Vocabulary gap between our terms and theirs.

evidence.excerpt: I think we had the better product online. I still think that.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Rep's belief about online product superiority.

contradictions.what: Rep named Raj as final decider and ran-the-RFP contact, then said Angela signed with Adyen and hedged to 'Probably Angela'.
Rep says they were ahead before the workshop, yet also says they never had store capability and knew it was lost after workshop.
Rep says the deal was about web strength, but the trigger was store returns and customer questions moved to stores.
Our pitch said unified commerce; rep says the customer never used that term and wanted tills.

dodges.question: What did you say?
dodges.what: Answered 'I described it' without saying what he said to Bev's till return question; later admits no demo.

dodges.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
dodges.what: Named Raj with no evidence of how he knew; later revealed Angela signed.

outcome_signals.what: Rep says the web side was won before the workshop, but the customer signed with Adyen overall; unclear what moved to us.
Rep knew it was lost after the store ops workshop.
